blockAssessments.assessment: Nonzero signed probe charge and uniform static E are explicit. Displacement is along E with positive separation. Dot-product work equals q*E*d for either charge sign; q cancellation is valid. V=U1-U2 gives a positive potential drop for nonzero E and d, whereas negative-charge work is negative. Force direction is not confused with field direction.

Comparisons hold at the same along-field distance. Spatially constant potential implies zero full E; a constant value in only one direction determines only its corresponding component. The finite-distance relation is a local approximation in a continuous nonsingular static field with negligible directional and magnitude variation, not an arbitrary-field exact equality.

The SI operational definition includes along-field separation and endpoint order. V/m=(J/C)/m=N/C. The historical conversion uses the source rounded volt factor and centimetre conversion, yielding1/(300*100)=1/(3*10^4); prose explicitly disclaims exactness of the rounded conversion. All original math atoms remain unchanged.

Each infinitesimal tangential displacement is transverse to the local static E, so its work contribution is zero. A path-connected smooth surface with that property has constant potential. Uniform-field surfaces are parallel planes and point-charge surfaces concentric spheres. Normality and decreasing-potential direction are restricted to regular nonzero-field locations; infinity is a specified reference for the positive point-charge illustration.

The conductor is the same connected body in electrostatic equilibrium. The material interior has zero E, the external surface-adjacent tangential component vanishes, and its potential is constant. The solid isolated spherical conductor is undisturbed and in the same homogeneous-medium model with infinity reference. The potential evaluated at the surface radius is also the interior constant; an interior observation radius must not be substituted into the exterior point-charge expression.
All four original figure slots and all four captions remain exactly bound. This textual science review creates no source-image inventory, geometry decision, visual approval or figure promotion.

independentDerivations: A=q integral E dot dl=q E d for constant E and parallel displacement. Electrostatic work is q(U1-U2); nonzero q cancels even if negative. Hence E=(U1-U2)/d. Only the work sign changes with probe sign.

For a short displacement, dU=-E dot dl. A directional zero derivative removes one component only; zero gradient throughout a spatial region removes all components. Curvature/magnitude variation leaves a higher-order finite-step error, so the modern text correctly states local approximation.

On an equipotential tangent, dU=0 and E dot dl=0. At a regular point E is normal to its constant-potential surface. The static connected conductor has no internal field; integrating along paths inside its material gives equal potentials.

The approved source equation8-28 gives the spherical exterior potential in its medium. Evaluating at the conductor radius gives the constant interior potential without treating interior observation points as exterior radii.
